macro.text: A reported Khamenei call to end Iran's "neither war nor peace" stance moved markets a little.
Stock futures rise as earnings season continues.
The Fed is expected to hold rates steady this week, but Warsh may point the way to more hikes.
Oil prices seesaw amid renewed diplomatic efforts to end the Mideast conflict.
Tech stocks rally as the AI trade revives.
Nvidia to invest $3 billion in Meta as the two deepen their AI partnership.

briefs.read: The tone is risk-on, led by tech: QQQ is up about 1.5% premarket at 714.79 and SPY about 0.9% at 767.05, both above yesterday's closes, while the VIX closed lower near 17.9 and WTI is down about 0.7% near $101 with the 10-year yield flat near 4.99%. There is no high-impact U.S. release today; the only red events are Australian CPI at 8:30 PM ET and the RBNZ rate decision at 9:00 PM ET, both after the U.S. close, so the session is driven by earnings (Boeing, Coca-Cola, UPS before the open) and headlines. The bigger scheduled event is the Fed decision later this week, where a hold is expected but rate-hike guidance from Warsh is the open question. Before taking a setup, it is worth waiting for the first 15-minute range to form and seeing whether QQQ's large premarket gap holds at the open, and keeping an eye on Iran diplomacy headlines, which can move oil and the indexes quickly.

CNBC survey: Fed rate hikes are coming, but not this week.

briefs.read: The morning's risk-on tone has faded rather than flipped: SPY at 765.70 is only +0.04% on the day and QQQ at 714.62 is +0.34%, both slightly below their 9:30 opens (-0.21% and -0.07%) and SPY under its 767.05 premarket print, with QQQ about level with its 714.79 premarket print (this morning's premarket percentages were measured against the wrong close; the real gap up was about +0.2% for SPY and +0.4% for QQQ). The VIX is lower at 17.77 (-3.4%), the 10-year yield has edged up to 5.00%, and WTI is slightly lower near $101.24, flat since the open. There is still no U.S. red event today (calendar check failed this run; the morning list had only Australian CPI at 8:30 PM ET and the RBNZ decision at 9:00 PM ET), and the Fed meeting that started today is the week's main event.
